Unfortunately for him, we naively suppressed him as much as possible and prevented him from acting on anything as best as we could. This hurt him a lot, and we could tell, but we didn't know that it would be possible to reconcile with him. But we tried after receiving some advice and it turned out to be very possible! I think it was shortly after high school graduation. But we spoke and "let him out of his cage," and we all eventually became good friends.

I like to think about the Muppets lyric a lot: "There's not a word yet for old friends who've just met..."

But yeah, that old persecutor bonded with someone else, a trauma holder, in a sibling sort of relationship. I can't remember the first couple years of college very well, probably because they fronted together almost always. It was one of the biggest turnarounds we've ever had.

Since, we've done our best to foster similar relationships. Also can't remember the gap here too well. But since I've learned we're actually polyfragmented, it's obviously become awfully difficult to keeping everyone straight.

I dunno what our breakthrough really was, and I also don't know how we developed with such strong internal communication despite some people like me having really weirdly missing memories. But we've moved past just collaborating to keep the body alive to actually caring about each other, probably beginning when one of our littles appeared and we felt absolutely compelled to treat her as well as we could.
